reason: The cited evidence directly supports each premise: E1 describes laser cladding's strong bonding and Ti(C,N)'s combined properties; E2 and E3 show in situ ceramic phases in nickel-based coatings improve hardness and wear resistance on titanium alloys, though the specific Ni+Ti(C,N) system on TC4 is not directly demonstrated.
premises: Laser cladding can produce coatings with strong metallurgical bonding on titanium alloys
Ti(C,N) combines high hardness from TiC and toughness from TiN, yielding high wear resistance
In situ synthesized ceramic phases bond better and distribute more evenly than mechanically added ones
Nickel-based composite coatings with ceramic phases can be fabricated by laser cladding
Such coatings can significantly increase hardness and wear resistance of titanium alloy substrates
